meta.title: Why David Hume says you can't prove the sun will rise

Caspar David Friedrich night landscape moon

beats.text: The sun has risen every morning of your life. So it will rise tomorrow. Obvious, right?
David Hume asked a dangerous question: how do you actually know that?
You have seen the past. You have never once seen the future. Those are not the same thing.
To say the future will resemble the past, you'd have to assume the very thing you're trying to prove.
No experiment can escape it. Every prediction smuggles in a leap that reason cannot justify.
So why do we trust tomorrow at all? Not logic, Hume said — habit. Custom. The mind's reflex.
Almost everything you 'know' about the world rests on a faith reason can never fully earn.

attribution: David Hume · An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
